t: The first government to unite the whole of Pohnpei, ruling from Nan Madol, a complex of nearly a hundred artificial islets of stacked basalt.
Its history is known from Pohnpeian oral tradition and archaeology; its dates and even the number of its rulers are uncertain.
Tradition says the hero Isokelekel overthrew the last Saudeleur around 1628 and founded the Nahnmwarki chiefdoms that survive today.
dyk: Uranium-thorium dating of coral from the tomb of Pohnpei’s first island-wide ruler places its building at about 1180–1200, before monument building began on most other Pacific islands.
ev: First traces of human activity at the site of Nan Madol
Building of artificial islets on the reef at Nan Madol is under way
By tradition, Olosohpa becomes the first Saudeleur and unites Pohnpei
The tomb of Pohnpei’s first island-wide ruler is built at Nan Madol
Most of Nan Madol’s palaces, temples and tombs are built
Isokelekel overthrows the last Saudeleur, Saudemwohl, and becomes the first Nahnmwarki
Nan Madol becomes a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is listed as in danger
